title: Agent Loop — Inside a Coding Agent
description: A step-through simulation of an AI coding agent working a ticket: a circular Plan → Read → Edit → Run tests → Observe → Done diagram lights up while a scripted transcript, a live diff and a test panel go from red to green. Play, pause, step, change speed, and switch between fixing a failing test, adding a feature test-first, and a refactor that catches its own regression.
prompt: Build me a single-file, animated explainer of what a coding agent actually does when it fixes a bug. I want a circular loop diagram — Plan, Read, Edit, Run tests, Observe, Done — that lights up as a scripted session plays in a terminal pane, next to a file-diff pane and a test-results pane that goes red to green. Give it play/pause, step, speed and restart controls, three scenarios (fix a failing test, add a feature, refactor with tests), and running token and tool-call counters. Keep it purely scripted: no network, no model calls, and make the scripts realistic enough that an engineer nods along.

methodology: State-machine testing: every scenario is a fixed script, so the oracle for any step N is known in advance (active loop node, test summary, counters) and asserted via data-testid/data-active attributes rather than colours.
Timing isolated with page.clock: Play is verified by advancing the fake clock and checking step progression, pause stability, and auto-stop at the final step.
Cumulative-counter checks: tokens and tool calls are asserted at exact values after specific steps and after Restart to catch double-counting on re-render.
Scenario isolation: switching scenarios mid-run must reset step, counters and test list to the new script's shape (3 vs 4 tests).
Content oracles on the diff pane: added/removed lines are exposed with diff-add/diff-del test ids so the edit step is checked for the actual code change, not just visibility.
Visual review at 1280px and 390px for the SVG diagram, terminal overflow and diff horizontal scrolling.
risks: Play timer racing a manual Step or scenario switch, leading to double advances or a zombie timeout after restart.
Derived state drift: counters or test statuses computed incrementally instead of replayed from the script would diverge after restart.
Long diff lines forcing horizontal page scroll on narrow phones.
Comet rotation spinning backwards or accumulating wrongly when the phase jumps around the loop.
qa.playwright: Stepping was trivial to automate because the page renders all state from a pure replay of the script, so every assertion hangs off data-testid and data-active attributes. The hard part was Play: page.clock.install() on its own keeps the fake clock ticking in real time, so exact step counts after runFor() were flaky on a loaded machine (one mobile run overshot to the end). The fix was install() followed by clock.pauseAt(), so only runFor() moves time; the spec then asserts exact counts, pauses, and proves that another 5 s of fake time changes nothing. The SVG loop is checked through attributes on each node group, not pixels, so toHaveScreenshot was deliberately avoided — the comet and pulse animations would make snapshots noisy. Diff content is asserted by text on diff-add/diff-del rows, which is a stronger oracle than a screenshot.
coverage: Step through the full 'fix' scenario: plan → failing run → … → done, summary red then green, Step disabled at end
Edit step renders one removed and one added line with the exact fix
Token and tool-call counters accumulate exactly and reset on Restart
Play at 2× speed advances on the fake clock, Pause holds position, playback auto-stops at 10/10
Switching scenarios resets progress and loads the TDD script whose new tests fail first

a11y: All controls are native buttons and a labelled select, with Space/→/R shortcuts that don't hijack focused controls; the transcript is a role="log" live region and each step is also announced through a polite live region. Test statuses carry screen-reader text in addition to colour and icon.
